title: Multi-session longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset (Kumar et al. 2024)
description: A longitudinal motor imagery EEG dataset from 18 BCI-naive participants recorded across six sessions (one offline, five online) with left/right hand motor imagery and continuous visual feedback. It was collected to study transfer learning for acquiring BCI skills, comparing unsupervised Generic Recentering and supervised Personally Assisted Recentering for calibration-free training. Data comprise 22 EEG channels sampled at 512 Hz and were processed with Riemannian geometry-based classifiers.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 18 healthy subjects over 6 sessions with ANT Neuro eego mylab (22 EEG and 3 EOG channels, 512 Hz). Subjects performed cue-based left/right hand motor imagery with bar-feedback runs and car racing games; session 1 had 4 offline runs (80 trials) and sessions 2-6 had 3-4 online runs each. Signals were bandpass filtered 8-30 Hz (second-order Butterworth), covariance features were extracted, and a Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean decoder was used.
